source_caption:
Airplane! (1980) is widely seen as one of the most important parody films ever made, helping redefine what spoof comedy could be. The movie was loosely inspired by the serious disaster film Zero Hour! and also poked fun at popular 1970s disaster movies like Airport.

The story follows Ted Striker, played by Robert Hays, a former fighter pilot who’s terrified of flying. When the flight crew and many passengers get sick from food poisoning, he’s forced to face his fears and try to land the plane himself. On the ground, he gets help from Dr. Rumack, played by Leslie Nielsen, whose completely serious delivery makes the absurd jokes land even harder.

Instead of building tension like a traditional disaster movie, Airplane! fires off nonstop jokes, mixing wordplay, visual gags, and ridiculous situations delivered with straight faces. Its rapid-fire humor and unforgettable one-liners turned it into a true comedy classic, and its style went on to influence countless parody films that followed.

source_details.synopsis: Airplane! (alternatively titled Flying High!) is a 1980 American comedy film written and directed by David Zucker, Jim Abrahams, and Jerry Zucker in their directorial debut, and produced by Jon Davison. It stars Robert Hays and Julie Hagerty and features Leslie Nielsen, Robert Stack, Lloyd Bridges, Peter Graves, Lorna Patterson, Stephen Stucker, and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. It is a parody of the disaster film genre, particularly the 1957 Paramount film Zero Hour!, from which it borrows the plot, central characters, and some dialogue.
